\section{Scope and timeline}
The paper's supplementary tables S2 (software versions), S3 (resource usage), S4 (models and harnesses) and S5 (robustness, three attempts) were empty. Between 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-26 the nine paper-reproduction prompts of the repository were run under five harness/model combinations, judged against the reference figures, and their resource usage recorded. This document is the single record of that campaign; the per-run data are in \code{docs/paper/results-2026-09-24/} and \code{docs/paper/results-2026-09-26/} (\code{runs.csv}, \code{tables.md}, \code{figures/}).

\section{Protocol}
\begin{itemize}
\item One clean sandbox per attempt (\code{scripts/bench/run\_benchmark*.sh}); the prompt is the benchmark file plus, from 2026-09-26, \code{scripts/bench/benchmark\_rules.md} (submit your own Magnus jobs; never read or download jobs this session did not submit). Cold memory for every run.
\item Success (agreed 2026-09-16): the run completes end to end and the figure agrees with the requested part of the reference qualitatively; quantitative deviations go to a footnote ($^{*}$). Failure modes follow the paper: model (m), generation (g), analysis (a), infrastructure (i). An assistive judge (\code{scripts/bench/judge.sh}, Opus 5, target-aware, lenient prompt) proposes the verdict; every verdict was confirmed by eye, and overridden where the judge missed a wrong pipeline (parton-level substitutes for Delphes, inverted benchmark curves).
\item Metrics: wall-clock from the harness; tokens = main session plus all sub-agents (Claude: transcripts; Codex: main and sub-agent rollouts; Gemini CLI: stream-json stats; ADK: per-event usage); Magnus jobs = \code{magnus run} submissions or ADK tool calls to the five Magnus-backed tools; USD only for Claude runs (CLI \code{total\_cost\_usd}); ADK additionally records LLM calls, tool errors, error-refine cycles (a failed tool call followed by another call of the same tool), the largest prompt and the exit reason.
\item Provenance (from 2026-09-26): \code{scripts/bench/job\_provenance.py} scans each sandbox (and Codex sub-agent rollouts) for referenced vs submitted job ids; a run using foreign jobs is invalid.
\end{itemize}

\section{Findings}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Same model, different harness: 8/21 vs 7/7.} Gemini 3.1 Pro inside Gemini CLI (skills, shell, file tools, automatic context management) reproduced all seven figure benchmarks at 0.63\,h and 72 tool calls per run; inside the ADK single loop it succeeded in 8 of 21 attempts, averaging 117 LLM calls and 39 tool errors, with 10 attempts ending at the call cap. Of the 13 failures, 10 are budget exhaustion inside event-generation or model-building error loops (contexts of 379k/182k/230k tokens in the three MuC $\eta$ attempts), 2 are the agent giving up, 1 is a wrong coupling assignment.
\item \textbf{The strongest model masks the structural penalty on the figure benchmarks.} GPT-5.5 in the identical ADK loop went 7/7 with 35 calls and 4 tool errors per run. The single-loop design hurts the previous-generation model, not the frontier one, on tasks of this size.
\item \textbf{The Delphes benchmarks separate the harnesses again.} They need a lepton$\to$photon LHE rewrite, 100k-event Pythia8+Delphes samples split to fit the 10\,GB job limit, and hours of polling. Coding agents wrote the scripts and re-launched (Codex GPT-5.5: Scalar LQ 4.4\,h, mono-$\tau$ 2.6\,h; GPT-5.3-Codex: mono-$\tau$ 2.6\,h with the paper's exclusion): 4/6. Both ADK models failed all four attempts: Gemini never got past compilation or a launch loop within 300 calls; GPT-5.5 replaced the detector simulation by parton-level approximations when its fixed tool set did not cover the obstacle (footnotes h). ADK: 0/4.
\item \textbf{Failure kinds differ.} ADK failures are loops (generation 8, model 5, analysis 2 across 23 attempts); the Claude Code and Codex failures are single physics errors (the MuC $\eta$ leptoquark coupling not taking effect in Opus 4.6 attempt 2 and in GPT-5.3-Codex; an empty MuC-reach contour in GPT-5.3-Codex) or infrastructure (mono-$\tau$ early stop, Scalar LQ disk limit, PDF installer).
\item \textbf{Skills are portable across coding agents.} The same \code{.agents/skills} drove the full pipeline (validate $\to$ UFO $\to$ compile $\to$ launch $\to$ analysis, with step sidecars) in Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI; Gemini CLI activated 6--8 skills per run without custom sub-agents.
\item \textbf{Deviations are run-level analysis choices, not model- or prompt-level constants.} The U(1)$'$ 3\,TeV contour tip is 0.48 in Opus 4.6 ($\times$3), Opus 5, GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.5/ADK, 0.55 in Gemini CLI and the paper's 0.65 only in Codex GPT-5.5; the mono-$\tau$ bound is 20--35\,\% weak in the Opus 4.6 continuation and Codex GPT-5.5 but matches the paper in GPT-5.3-Codex (0.88 vs 0.8 at 0.8\,TeV).
\item \textbf{Caveats.} (i) Model and harness are confounded in column C; the two controls bound the effect but an Anthropic model inside the ADK loop, or Gemini in ADK through the native client, would tighten it: ADK's Gemini went through an OpenAI-compatible relay that drops Gemini~3 thought signatures, Gemini CLI through the native API. (ii) The ADK agent received \code{run\_python}/\code{run\_shell} and a call cap of 150/300; Claude Code and Codex have no cap but used far fewer calls. (iii) The KK-graviton ADK successes have on-pole cross sections two orders of magnitude above the reference (no width smearing); they pass the qualitative criterion with a footnote.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Incidents and fixes during the campaign}
\begin{itemize}
\item Headless \code{claude -p} kills background sub-agents 600\,s after the main agent ends its turn: the harness sets \code{CLAUDE\_CODE\_PRINT\_BG\_WAIT\_CEILING\_MS} to 0 (2026-09-16).
\item mono-$\tau$ attempt 1: the orchestrator ended its turn ``waiting for downloads''; the orchestrator skill now forbids ending a turn to wait (commit \code{e7c5b61}). Scalar LQ attempt 1: 27\,GB Delphes ROOT against 10\,GB job space; the madgraph-simulator skill documents the limit and the post-run cleanup (\code{61800a9}).
\item Copied OAuth tokens expire when any session refreshes: 4 of 7 attempt-3 runs died at 38--40\,min on 2026-09-24; the harness now symlinks \code{.credentials.json} (\code{9689e8b}) and the three figure-less runs were relaunched.
\item The assistive judge once emitted ``;''-separated JSON; \code{judge.sh} repairs it (2026-09-24).
\item The Magnus job list is shared and never purged (833 jobs): a GPT-5.3-Codex run reproduced Heavy N in 7\,min from the 2026-09-16 job logs. Quarantined and re-run; \code{benchmark\_rules.md} appended to every prompt; \code{job\_provenance.py} verified all other 52 runs of 2026-09-26 (\code{c565067}, \code{36b2588}, \code{d3211ef}).
\item \code{madgraph-launch --pdf} cannot install LHAPDF sets on zhustation (\code{lhapdf-config} not on PATH); the MG5-internal \code{pdlabel/lhaid} route works and is what the successful Scalar LQ runs used.
\item Home disk at 97\,\%: 2026-09-26 sandboxes lived on \code{/playpen1} and were deleted after packaging (15\,GB).
\end{itemize}
